questions.question: Who is responsible for labeling hazardous materials correctly?
questions.explanation: The shipper must package, mark, and label hazardous materials properly. The driver should verify the materials are labeled correctly.

questions.question: What do you do if a hazardous material label is too large for the package?

options.text: The label may be placed on a tag securely attached to the package.
A scannable QR code may instead be attached to the package.
The HazMat label should be reduced in size to fit on the package.
The label may be pasted to the wall of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The label may be placed on a tag securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: If a label does not fit on a package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: Where should you load hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Heat can make many materials more dangerous.

questions.question: When transporting explosives, where may you leave your vehicle unattended?
questions.explanation: You may only leave your vehicle unattended in a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved location for parking vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: Where should hazardous materials shipping papers be when the driver is not in the vehicle?
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be easy to find. Leave hazardous materials shipping papers on the driver's seat when you leave the vehicle.

questions.question: How should hazardous materials be loaded and unloaded?
questions.explanation: Heat makes many hazardous materials more dangerous. Load and unload hazardous materials away from heat sources.

questions.question: How are hazardous materials warnings shown?

options.text: By wrapping the package in orange
By placing the item away from other cargo and covering it with a sign

questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs called placards are placed on vehicles and bulk packages to warn others about hazardous materials.

questions.question: What can you do with an improperly placarded vehicle?

options.text: May only be moved in an emergency.
May be driven if the cargo is not radioactive.

questions.correctAnswerText: May only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle without proper placards for its hazardous materials can only be moved in an emergency to protect lives and property.

questions.question: Which agency must check your background for a HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: To get a new or renewed hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass a background check from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: What do you need to know to choose the right placards?

options.text: The hazard classes of the materials.
The types of containers holding the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard classes of the materials.
questions.explanation: To pick the right placards, you must know the hazard class of the materials, the amount being shipped, and the total weight of all hazardous materials in the vehicle.

questions.question: Explosive materials are classified as a ____ hazard.
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials can cause explosions or fires.

questions.question: Flammable gases are classified as ____ hazards.
questions.explanation: Flammable gases are Class 2 hazardous materials.

questions.question: If hazardous material cargo is leaking and the driver has no phone, they should:

options.text: Drive to find a phone and call emergency personnel.
Drive to a hazardous materials clean-up facility.
Send someone else to get help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Send someone else to get help.
questions.explanation: Do not drive the vehicle if cargo is leaking. More area will become contaminated. Park the vehicle, secure it, stay with it, and contact emergency personnel. If you have no phone, send someone else to get help.

questions.question: Which letters must appear on the shipping paper and package for a reportable quantity substance?
questions.explanation: The letters "RQ" must appear on the shipping paper and package for reportable quantity hazardous materials.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class show?

options.text: How fast the material must be delivered

questions.explanation: A hazard class shows the risks of a hazardous material. There are nine hazard classes total.

questions.question: Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table lists:
questions.explanation: Column 2 lists the proper shipping names and descriptions of regulated materials.

questions.question: A hazardous materials warning placard is shaped like a:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on the shipping paper, which placard must be shown?

options.text: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on shipping papers or packages, display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard.

questions.question: How many identical placards must be on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: A vehicle must have four identical placards: one on the front, one on the back, and one on each side.

questions.question: A shipping paper:

options.text: Is not needed for most hazardous materials shipments
Is required for all hazardous materials shipments
Can be stored as a digital file only

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required for all hazardous materials shipments
questions.explanation: Shipping papers are required for all hazardous materials shipments to communicate the material risks.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. Only keep it running if you need it to operate a pump.

questions.question: When transporting hazardous materials, placards:

options.text: Should only be used with explosives.
Should be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.
Should only be used by Class A licensed drivers.
Should be used to lower insurance costs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards must be displayed on all four sides of any vehicle carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: A driver should make sure that:

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on the packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.
The shipping paper is not in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on the packages.
questions.explanation: Compare the shipping paper to the markings and labels on each package. The shipping paper description must match what is marked and labeled on the packages.

questions.question: Emergency response information from the shipper must include:

options.text: Any risks of fire or explosion.
How many people should respond to an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any risks of fire or explosion.
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include the material names, health hazards, fire and explosion risks, actions to take in an accident, how to handle fires, how to handle spills, and first aid steps.

questions.question: If a leak is suspected in radioactive material cargo:

options.text: The driver should go to the local fire department.
The driver should pick up any loose pieces of radioactive material.
The driver should continue driving and avoid touching the affected areas.
The driver should stop and not drive the vehicle until it is cleaned.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver should stop and not drive the vehicle until it is cleaned.
questions.explanation: Tell your dispatcher or supervisor right away if you suspect a leak in radioactive material. Do not touch or breathe the material. Do not use the vehicle until it has been cleaned and checked with a survey meter.

questions.question: A person should not smoke within ____ of a vehicle with a Class 3 or Division 2.1 placard.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a placarded cargo tank carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: Who must provide emergency response information?
questions.explanation: The shipper of hazardous materials must provide emergency response information to the driver.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves on a compressed gas tank closed. Open them only when loading or unloading.

questions.question: If a product requires a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard, it must be used when transporting:

options.text: More than 50 pounds of the product.
More than 10 pounds of the product.
The product in a non-sealed container.

questions.explanation: The "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard and the correct hazard class placard must be displayed for all amounts of these materials.

questions.question: A hazardous material's identification number should appear:

options.text: On a sticker near the shipping container.

questions.explanation: The ID number must appear on the shipping paper and on the packaging. It must also appear on cargo tanks and other bulk packaging.
